fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Vehicle Parking Area; Walkway; Landscaped Area; Dense Vegetation; Open Lawn Area; Detached Structure; Perimeter Fencing; Patio Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance so responders can identify the property quickly from the road.
• Trim vegetation along both sides of the driveway so emergency vehicles can travel its full length without obstruction.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the main residence to create a clear gap between plants and the structure's exterior walls.
• Thin dense vegetation areas so responders can move through or around the property without being blocked.
• Keep a gate, door, or opening in the perimeter fencing accessible from the front so responders can reach the rear of the property on foot.
• Mark or label any rear gate latch from the outside so responders can locate and operate it quickly under low-light or high-stress conditions.
• Keep the patio area clear of stored items so it can serve as a staging area for equipment or personnel.
• Confirm the detached structure is labeled or numbered visibly from the driveway so responders can distinguish it from the main residence during an emergency.
• If the perimeter fencing has a single lockable gate, consider installing a Knox Box or rapid-access lock so responders are not delayed gaining entry.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Large Trees; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Vegetation Separation; Vegetation Along Driveway; Open Green Space; Single Access Route; Woody Debris
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back all shrubs and plants that are directly touching or within a few feet of the house walls.
• Thin trees around the house to create open gaps between their canopy edges and the structure.
• Remove dead branches, fallen limbs, and any woody debris piled near or around the house.
• Thin the tree clusters near the house so individual trees are separated from each other and from the structure.
• Trim lower branches off large trees near the house up to about 10 feet from the ground.
• Clear shrubs and low-growing plants from under scattered trees near the structure.
• Cut back or remove vegetation growing along both sides of the driveway to keep it passable for vehicles.
• Trim any tree branches that hang over the driveway so emergency vehicles can pass without obstruction.
• Clear woody debris from the driveway edges so the full width of the road surface stays open.
• Keep the single access route free of fallen branches, overgrown brush, and any other obstructions year-round.
• Remove or thin dense shrubs and plants between the house and the driveway to keep that path open.
• Collect and remove all woody debris, brush piles, and dead plant material from around the house and outbuildings.
• Separate any tree canopies that currently touch or overlap near the structure so fire cannot travel directly between
